property_summary: After owner calls sudicideAnyone(), the contract's code remains intact (it does not destroy itself), but the buggy version reverts inappropriately, so a call to sudicideAnyone() should succeed (no revert) on the reference and fail (revert) on the buggy version.

After a call to sudicideAnyone() by the owner, the contract's code must remain empty (self-destructed) so that a subsequent call to any contract function reverts or has no code; the buggy version leaves the code intact, so a subsequent call does not revert.
After any successful owner call to sudicideAnyone(), address(c).balance must be zero (ether transferred to owner); the buggy version reverts the call leaving the balance unchanged.
After a successful call to sudicideAnyone() by the owner, the contract c must have no code (self-destructed); the buggy version reverts, leaving the contract code intact.
After a successful owner call to sudicideAnyone(), the contract must have no code (self-destructed); the buggy version reverts leaving the contract code intact.

After any call to sudicideAnyone by any caller, the contract C must be destroyed (its code size becomes zero). The mutant allows any caller to trigger selfdestruct, so the reference holds for the owner but the buggy version also selfdestructs for a non-owner, making the property fail for non-owner calls.
For any caller, call to sudicideAnyone succeeds (does not revert) if and only if the caller is the owner; the bug removes the only-owner check so a non-owner call incorrectly succeeds.
After a call to sudicideAnyone made by the owner, the contract must be destroyed (code size becomes 0) in the reference version, but the buggy version leaves it alive (code size remains > 0).
After the owner calls sudicideAnyone, the reference contract's code size becomes 0 (destroyed), but the buggy version keeps code size > 0 because the selfdestruct was removed.
After the owner calls sudicideAnyone, the contract's code size must become 0 (destroyed) in the reference version, but the buggy version leaves it non-zero because selfdestruct was removed.
After any owner call to sudicideAnyone, the contract must be destroyed (code size zero), but the buggy version leaves it alive with non-zero code size.
After calling sudicideAnyone, the contract balance must always become zero; the buggy selfdestruct targeting address(0) fails to destroy the contract, so address(c).balance remains non-zero.
After a successful selfdestruct, the contract's code must be empty; the buggy version targeting address(0) fails and leaves code intact, so address(c).code.length is non-zero.

After any owner call to sudicideAnyone, the contract must be destroyed (selfdestruct) — in the reference, the contract is gone; in the bug, selfdestruct to address(0) fails and the contract stays alive, so calling any public function on c thereafter must revert because the contract no longer exists in the reference but does in the bug.
For any owner, after calling sudicideAnyone, address(c) must have no code; the buggy version targeting address(0) fails selfdestruct, so address(c).code.length remains non-zero.

After any owner calls sudicideAnyone, the contract's balance must become zero, because the reference selfdestruct transfers all ether; the buggy version targeting address(0) fails to selfdestruct, so the contract's balance remains equal to its prior balance.
